transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve been really exhausted lately. Not just tired like I need a good night’s sleep, but worn out in a way that sleep doesn’t seem to fix. Even getting through a normal workday and then dinner at home feels a lot heavier than it should.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yes. Most days lately, I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling. It’s like I’m already disappointed in the day before it’s even really started.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes. I usually really enjoy painting, and I like wandering through museum exhibits, but lately I just don’t feel drawn to any of it. My paints are just sitting there untouched, and even the idea of going to a museum feels like too much effort. I can’t really make myself care about it right now.
Did this start after a major stressor or life change?
Not that I can clearly point to. I’ve been trying to think if something set it off, but there wasn’t one big change or event that I can identify. It just sort of crept up on me.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I... I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself making plans to hurt myself or anything like that. I guess I just feel really low, but I don’t know that I’d say life isn’t worth living.
Before this current period, have you ever had another episode in your life when you felt depressed and lost interest in things in a similar way?
Yes, I have. The longest time I can clearly remember was about five months. I felt depressed most days, really tired, and just not like myself.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?
I’m not sure I’d say excessively. I do worry about things, but I haven’t really noticed it being about a lot of different things all the time.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes. I can usually get to bed at a reasonable time, but I’ve been waking up around four or five in the morning. Then I start thinking about work or my marriage, and after that I just can’t get back to sleep.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes, I have. At work, even with something simple like a staffing email, I’ll just sit there rereading it over and over. I can’t seem to decide what to say or which option makes sense, and it takes me way longer than it should.
Have you noticed a decrease in your appetite lately?
Yes, a bit. I’ve been kind of picking at meals, and sometimes I forget to eat lunch when I’m at work. I’ve noticed my skirts are fitting a little looser, and I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Yes, I think so. My staff has noticed it too—like in meetings, when someone asks me a question, there’s this pause before I can get my thoughts together and actually answer. It’s like my words are moving slower than usual.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable for several days in a row?

Yes. Earlier this month I had a few days where I felt really charged up and upbeat, like I was full of ideas and everything made sense. But then I’d also get irritated really quickly, especially if my husband questioned what I was planning.
During those few days when you felt charged up and upbeat, did you need much less sleep than usual?
Yes. I was only sleeping maybe four hours a night during that stretch, but I’d still wake up feeling ready to go—like I should send emails, sketch out event ideas, or reorganize the kitchen.
During those days when you felt especially charged up, did you feel unusually confident or important?

Yes, I did. At the time I really believed I could fix the whole morale problem at work, and also get our family routines sorted out, if everyone would just listen to my plan and get on board. It felt very clear to me then.
During those charged-up days, were you talking more than usual?
Yes. My husband noticed it, and a couple of coworkers did too. They said I was talking really fast and kind of jumping in so much that they couldn’t really get a word in.
During those charged-up days, did your behavior cause serious problems at work, at home, or with other people?

Not serious problems, exactly. I’m still getting to work and taking care of things at home. But I have noticed I’ve been slower making decisions, less dependable with family plans, and I’ve pulled back from the art stuff I usually do to stay connected with people.
During those charged-up days, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might have been more pushy with my ideas, but I can’t think of anything really risky or impulsive that I did.
How many days in a row did that charged-up, upbeat period last?
The whole swing has been going on about a month — starting with that unusually energized, driven stretch and then moving into feeling low.
Did that unusually energized, driven period last at least four days in a row?
Yes, it did. That whole shift has been going on about a month, and the energized, driven part was at the start of it.
During that energized stretch, were you more active than usual in starting or taking on projects?

Yes. I definitely took on more than I usually would. I signed myself up to lead extra parts of the morale program at work, and I volunteered for more Latino arts events too. At the time it felt doable, but looking back, it was a lot more than I’d normally commit to.
